### Evaluation proposal

BoundaryScore is a proposed reference for a later check that internal spaces and
token boundaries survive preparation. No such evaluation has been run or added

### Alternative decision

PreserveSpaces is kept as an alternative, not adopted. This project currently
prefers trimming at row boundaries for simpler inputs. Whether leading/trailing
spaces carry meaningful data in a later task remains unresolved; no measured
comparison with preservation is available.

## Selected works and source passages

These source-note excerpts are the complete supplied paper evidence. Each title
heading provides a direct entry; none is a verified external paper identity.

### TrimBaseline

“TrimBaseline removes whitespace at the beginning and end of each row. Whitespace
between internal tokens is retained. The method does not decide whether boundary
whitespace is meaningful for a downstream task.”

### BoundaryScore

“BoundaryScore checks whether preparation changes internal token boundaries. It
compares token spans before and after preparation and reports altered boundaries;
it does not judge task accuracy or recommend a particular normalization method.”

### PreserveSpaces

“PreserveSpaces leaves leading and trailing whitespace untouched. It retains
boundary formatting that may carry meaning, but it does not remove accidental
padding or establish that preservation improves a downstream metric.”

### NeighborNotes

“NeighborNotes discusses ways to describe text preparation in research notes. It
does not specify a preprocessing implementation or an evaluation metric.”
